title: The Same Program, Another Simulator: One Backend Interface, the Built In Model Behind It, and Gazebo Sim Behind It Too

questions.question: Why a second simulator behind the same interface?
options: The built in one is too slow
To run two robots at once
A program tested on one has learnt that simulator's habits
Gazebo needs a reference to start
questions.explanation: Two let the answers be compared. With one simulator a program can come to depend on its quirks. With two behind one interface, the same script's answers can be laid side by side.

questions.question: Driving straight 5 s at 0.2 m/s from y = 2 ended on the built in backend at:
options: y = 3.000 exactly
y = 2.990, a little short of 3 because of the lag
questions.explanation: A metre is 0.2 m/s for 5 s. The lag of 0.05 s costs 0.05 times 0.2, a centimetre.

questions.question: A command of 5 m/s with a limit of 0.22 in the robot file gave:
options: 5 m/s, as commanded
0 m/s: it was refused
questions.explanation: The built in backend takes its limits from the robot file, 0.22 m/s and 2.84 rad/s.

questions.question: How is the Gazebo run made as long as it was asked to be?
options: The server is paused and stepped by the world control service until the clock gets there
It runs in real time and is timed with a clock
The program sleeps for the run's length
The run is cut when enough samples have arrived
questions.explanation: The run lasts as long in simulated time as was asked, however long the computer takes. Without that the two simulators could not be compared.

questions.question: Why does the Gazebo backend put itself in a partition of its own?
options: To use less memory
Because the world file needs a unique name
So the server starts paused
So that two runs, or two tests, never hear each other's messages
questions.explanation: gz-transport is shared between every process on the machine unless told otherwise. A private partition keeps one run's commands out of another's.

questions.question: What happens to the lesson on a machine without Gazebo?
options: It does not build
It builds and passes without the Gazebo test
It builds, and its tests are all skipped
It downloads Gazebo first
questions.explanation: The Gazebo backend and its test are built only where Gazebo is installed. Everything else in the lesson builds and passes without it.
